$comment: DRAFT icon grammar for ui-foundations-vault#45. This is a research artifact, NOT approved governance. Two independent axes are kept separate (D7): 'class' is the FIELD CLASSIFICATION of the rule, defined by HOW THE RULE IS DECIDED and NOT by how prevalent the observed convention is. hard = the rule is validated DETERMINISTICALLY regardless of prevalence (a near-universal convention does not make a rule hard, and a deterministically checkable convention is hard even if most assets violate it); heuristic = an APPROXIMATION comparing against observed values within an EXPLICIT numeric tolerance (every heuristic rule carries a concrete proposed numeric tolerance; no vague 'small'/'~' allowance may stand in for a tolerance); judgment = requires a HUMAN decision (rendered geometry, visual, or semantic). Where a rule has no numeric metric: it is 'hard' if automated presence detection IS the claimed deterministic rule, otherwise it is 'judgment' routed to human approval. Machine-checkability does NOT confer policy legitimacy. 'status' is the DRAFT LIFECYCLE of the rule in this artifact (always 'draft' here). 'evaluation' ties each rule to how it is decided: 'automated' means the audit tool decides it deterministically; 'manual' means it is surfaced for a human/visual decision and is never auto-passed. A rule is EITHER automated with a concrete criterion OR manual; there are no empty numeric tolerances attached to manual/heuristic rules, and every numeric tolerance below is an EXPLICIT proposed number (manual/unimplemented), not an executed check. Provenance keys: impl-guide = source/docs/agentic/icon-creation.md (status active, implementation convention only); usage-guide = source/site/patterns/icon.md (component usage scope); vault-pattern = vault/patterns/base/icon.pattern.md (derived draft). No source constitutes approved numeric governance. Nothing here promotes a repeated implementation convention to canonical approved governance, and no canonical governance is inferred from observed conventions.

provenance.input_source: src/assets/icons/*.svg (owned input; read by runtime scripts/generate-icon-list.mjs, invoked from build.mjs Stage 1)
provenance.external_brand_pdf: not supplied; no claim of external authority or manual design provenance is made
provenance.authority_note: Vault remains canonical governance. Implementation and usage guides are conventions, not approved numeric rules.

applicability.note: After PR66 a user-authored Figma design guideline (UI Assets Library, file Eprjc6hw7QyMvvD01eGgGy, section node 482:12945 'Icons') was supplied as a primary design source previously missing from the audit. The rules in the 'rules' array below compare assets ONLY to the runtime implementation/usage guides and are therefore scoped runtime-guide-only and marked provisional pending reconciliation with the Figma source. Existing audit_rule IDs are UNCHANGED; the tool does NOT execute any Figma rule. See figma-guideline-addendum.md. The separate machine-readable 'design_guideline_rules' array below records the Figma design constraints; it does not re-evaluate the 601 inventory and is not executed by the tool.

design_guideline_provenance.immutability_note: No immutable Figma version ID or commit SHA was obtained via MCP. Git commit SHAs do NOT version this Figma file; none is invented. Content snapshot text and capture SHA are supplied by Codex. The Figma file is unchanged.
design_guideline_provenance.authority_note: Vault remains canonical governance. This external Figma design source is referenced with provenance, not promoted to governance. Membership/mapping of the 601 runtime icons to this library and the applicable Figma revision are unresolved; the approved production mapping of the 601 icons is NOT conflated with this library.

design_guideline_rules.note: Nominal 24 agrees with the runtime-guide canvas size. Not re-evaluated against the 601 inventory.

design_guideline_rules.classification_note: Discrete documented size scale; deterministic membership can be checked after scope mapping. No approximate geometry tolerance or completed validation is implied.

design_guideline_rules.literal: strokes named 'stroke'; shapes needing fill named 'fill'
design_guideline_rules.note: Figma LAYER naming convention ('Naming for Coloring' post-it). This is NOT SVG filename naming and NOT a statement about XML attribute presence in exported SVGs. Read directly from the screenshot (structured context intercepted by a CodeConnect suggestion).

Example-layer bounds are OBSERVATIONS, not automatically normative keyshape bounding rules and not asserted equivalent to the actual keyshape frames. Inspect actual frames/export; NO automatic normalization is performed.

rules.statement: Root <svg> viewBox is '0 0 24 24'.
Root width and height are both '24'.
Root <svg> fill is 'none' (transparent canvas).

Circled variants use a centered 20x20 circle inside the 24x24 canvas. Two distinct circle path encodings are observed in the set (clockwise 'M12 22C...' and counter-clockwise 'M2 12C...'); neither is canonical.
rules.not_implemented_note: Geometry matching is not performed by the audit tool; this tolerance (proposed bbox/diameter absolute-error bound of 0.5 SVG user units) is a documented, manual/unimplemented proposal for a future rendered-geometry check, not an executed criterion.
rules.contradiction: impl-guide says to copy the circle path 'verbatim from plus-circled.svg', but checkmark-circled.svg uses a different circle encoding. Flagged, not reconciled.

rules.statement: Square keyshape is a centered 20x20 box; corner radius proposed at 0 with an explicit maximum.
rules.not_implemented_note: Geometry matching is not performed by the audit tool; this tolerance (proposed bbox absolute-error bound 0.5 and corner-radius maximum 1.0 SVG user units) is a documented, manual/unimplemented proposal only.

rules.statement: Wide containers use a vertically centered short rect.
rules.not_implemented_note: Geometry matching is not performed by the audit tool; this tolerance (proposed bbox absolute-error bound 0.5 SVG user units) is a documented, manual/unimplemented proposal only.

rules.statement: Tall containers use a horizontally centered narrow rect.
rules.not_implemented_note: Geometry matching is not performed by the audit tool; this tolerance (proposed bbox absolute-error bound 0.5 SVG user units) is a documented, manual/unimplemented proposal only.

rules.statement: Inner symbol is inset from the keyshape edge by a proposed 2 to 3 SVG user units. Depends on rendered geometry; requires visual review.
rules.not_implemented_note: The audit emits requires-visual-review for this rule; the inset bound (proposed 2 to 3 SVG user units) is a documented, manual/unimplemented proposal for a future rendered check, not an executed criterion.

rules.statement: The implementation guide states explicitly that every <path> uses stroke='#9747FF'. The audit compares each icon's effective stroke color to that documented value: '#9747FF' PASSES; any other concrete color is INCONSISTENT with the implementation guide. This is a convention conflict against the guide, not a production defect, because the guide is a convention and not approved governance.
rules.observed_distribution_note: The observed stroke-color distribution across the set (the reality is that most assets use '#333333', with only tui-extras.svg using '#9747FF') is reported separately in summary.json as a NON-NORMATIVE statistic. It is NOT the pass criterion. No 'dominant' color is treated as a pass. No color is labelled a 'placeholder' or 'authoring' color, because the guide does not describe '#9747FF' that way.

rules.statement: At render time the Icon component applies the SVG as a CSS mask-image with background-color: currentColor. Whether that technique neutralizes an asset's hardcoded literal color is a DIFFERENT SCOPE (component usage) that this asset-level audit does not test. The audit therefore emits requires-visual-review when an asset carries a hardcoded color, rather than inventing an approved exception to the asset-level color rule.
rules.scope_distinction: stroke.color = the literal color inside the SVG asset, compared to the guide's documented #9747FF. color.mask-applicability = whether the consuming component's CSS mask + currentColor changes the painted result at runtime. These are separate scopes; the asset rule is not waived by the usage behavior.
rules.no_invented_exception: There is no approved exception to the asset-level color rule. Marking the hardcoded color a 'documented-exception' on the basis of the mask technique would conflate the two scopes; it is not done. 0 documented exceptions is a valid outcome.

rules.statement: stroke-width is never set explicitly on any element (the SVG default of 1 applies). The audit checks for an explicit stroke-width on ANY element (path, g, svg) and for any path whose effective width comes from a non-initial source, so an inherited width from a <g stroke-width=...> is caught even when the path itself is bare.
Every drawn path has an effective stroke-linecap='round' (own, inherited, or resolved).
Every drawn path has an effective stroke-linejoin='round' (own, inherited, or resolved).

The fill attribute is OMITTED on every path (guide: 'Never use fill on any path'). The audit distinguishes the literal syntax (is a fill attribute present at all) from the effective paint model (does the fill paint anything): a path with a painting fill is inconsistent, AND a path carrying a literal fill attribute of any value, including fill='none', is also flagged as a syntax-level deviation. fill-rule/clip-rule='evenodd' may appear on closed compound shapes and are not fills.
Corner radii and internal spacing/alignment depend on rendered geometry and are not statically decidable. The audit emits requires-visual-review.
Optical centering/correction is a human visual decision; never auto-passed. The audit emits requires-visual-review.

Observed elements: svg, path, g, defs, clipPath, rect (rect only inside clipPath as a clip bound). No <style>, <image>, <use>, <mask>, gradients, or <text> observed in the snapshot. The allowed-element set is a proposed inventory, not a governed allowlist; the audit inventories element_counts rather than enforcing a fixed set.
rules.class_rationale: No numeric metric and no deterministic automated allow/deny rule is claimed (the tool inventories rather than enforces). Classified judgment for human approval of any future allowlist, not heuristic.

rules.statement: No raster/bitmap content; vector only.
Presence of a transform attribute is surfaced for review because effective geometry would need rendering. The audit emits requires-visual-review when a transform is present, otherwise pass.
rules.class_rationale: No numeric metric. The automated step is only presence detection, but the decision about whether a transform is acceptable needs rendered geometry; the rule is surfaced for a human (manual/requires-visual-review), so it is classified judgment, not heuristic.

rules.statement: A small number of icons wrap content in <g clip-path=url(#...)> with a <defs><clipPath><rect fill='white'/></clipPath></defs> clipping to the 24x24 bounds (an export artifact). Masks/clip-paths/defs are undocumented structural variants; the audit surfaces them in a requires-visual-review row rather than silently passing them as whole-structure compliance. It does NOT assert that vector-only structure equals full structure validation.
rules.class_rationale: No numeric metric. The tool detects presence of mask/clip/defs, but whether the clipping effect is acceptable needs human/rendered review; the row is manual/requires-visual-review, so it is classified judgment, not heuristic.

rules.statement: If an icon carries a <style> sheet, a class selector, a <use>/href reference, or an inline style this tool cannot resolve (custom properties, var(), functions), the audit cannot assert paint/geometry compliance and emits requires-visual-review. CSS-wide keywords (inherit/initial/unset/revert) and simple !important ARE resolved and recorded with how they resolved; they are never emitted as bare pseudo-values. The snapshot contains no <style> or <use>, so this row passes for the observed set, but the handling is honest about not evaluating such CSS when present.
rules.class_rationale: The claimed rule is deterministic automated PRESENCE detection of unevaluated CSS/references (no numeric metric and no approximation/tolerance). Per the class contract, automated presence detection being the rule makes it hard, not heuristic. It remains a convention, not approved governance.

rules.statement: LEXICAL syntax only: file names are lowercase kebab-case matching <object>[-variant][-modifier], allowing a single '--' segment. This rule judges the string shape, not the meaning of '--' (see naming.double-dash-semantics).

SEMANTIC judgement, separate from lexical syntax. The guide reserves '--' for rare dual-state icons and names exactly one: thumbs-up--down. The audit treats thumbs-up--down as a documented-exception; every other '--' name (arrow--left, chevron--down, aircraft--right, hand-pointing--left, ellipsis--vertical, arrow-circle--flip, and the -circled directional variants) uses '--' for a single direction or other meaning that the guide does NOT document, and is emitted as requires-visual-review for a semantic decision. These names are NOT auto-passed merely because the string is lexically valid.

Semantic meaning is carried only by the file name; no embedded semantic metadata (title/desc) exists in assets. Concept-to-name mapping is a human decision. The audit inventories title/desc/aria presence but does not decide semantic correctness.

Accessibility (aria-hidden for decorative, aria-label for meaningful) is applied by the consuming component, not the asset. Asset-level a11y metadata is intentionally absent; the audit emits guideline-gap at the asset layer.
No documented RTL/mirroring behavior for directional icons. Whether directional icons should mirror in RTL contexts is an unresolved guideline gap. The audit emits guideline-gap.

The guide states 'keyshape path first, then inner paths' AND cites shield-check.svg as 'checkmark path, then shield path' in the same breath. These contradict. Observed assets are inconsistent: checkmark-circled.svg draws the circle first; shield-check.svg draws the checkmark first. Path ordering cannot be auto-verified and is never auto-passed; the audit emits requires-visual-review.
contradiction_examples: shield-check.svg: checkmark path (M8 13L11 16.043L16 9) precedes the shield outline
checkmark-circled.svg: circle keyshape precedes the checkmark
star-circled.svg and plus-circled.svg: circle keyshape precedes the inner symbol

rules.statement: Filenames with -heavy/-bold/-ultrabold modifiers imply a heavier visual weight, but since stroke-width is never set explicitly the weight is achieved by geometry (doubled outlines), not by a stroke attribute. Heavy/bold filenames are NOT automatically exempted from any stroke/cap/join/width rule; the audit evaluates them like every other icon (there is no filename-based exemption in the tool).
